 Khaman Maluach 
 PHX 
 Center 
 #10 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Khaman Maluach amassed nine points (2-of-3 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Warriors.
 With Oso Ighodaro (oblique) sidelined, Maluach did not have to worry about a timeshare at center. He logged 28 minutes against the Warriors, recording a complete stat line and finishing one point and one rebound shy of a double-double. If the Suns had a good schedule, Ighodaro’s injury would make Maluach a more popular fantasy player. However, they have another two-game week in Week 2, so adding Maluach in 12-team leagues offers little upside. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Oso Ighodaro (oblique) has been ruled out against the Warriors on Saturday. 
 Ighodaro exited early from Wednesday’s game against Portland and was initially listed as doubtful for this one. Duop Reath should fill out the backup center minutes behind Khaman Maluach.

 Oso Ighodaro (oblique) is doubtful for Saturday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Ighodaro, initially believed to have suffered a hip injury during Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, has been diagnosed with an oblique strain. His absence on Saturday would likely result in Duop Reath playing rotation minutes off the bench, with Khaman Maluach remaining the starting center. 
 Khaman Maluach 
 PHX 
 Center 
 #10 
 Khaman Maluach tallied two points (1-of-2 FGs), six rebounds, one assist and one blocked shot in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Maluach started Wednesday’s season opener, but the second-year center did not rise to the occasion. He played 17 minutes, and that’s with backup Oso Ighodaro exiting just before halftime with a hip injury. While a popular sleeper pick in fantasy basketball, Wednesday was a reminder that Maluach will need time, especially when considering the lack of playing time as a rookie. 
 Oso Ighodaro 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #11 
 Oso Ighodaro (hip) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Ighodaro took a hit to his right hip during the second quarter of Wednesday’s game. Although he initially tried to play through the injury, the 7-footer was subbed out with just over a minute left in the half. Ighodaro didn’t return to the bench for the third quarter, and he’s done for the night. Khaman Maluach, who started Wednesday’s game, should play more minutes while Duop Reath slides into the back end of the rotation. 
 Oso Ighodaro 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #11 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Suns and Oso Ighodaro agreed to a three-year, $29 million extension. 
 The 40th overall pick in the 2024 draft, Ighodaro appeared in all 82 games for the Suns last season, starting 24. In those outings, he averaged 6.5 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 0.9 steals in 22.0 minutes per game. With Mark Williams sidelined due to injury, Ighodaro could begin the season as Phoenix’s starting center, with Khaman Maluach as his competition. Regardless of who wins the job, both will play rotation minutes. The contract gives Ighodaro added security, but that doesn’t change much regarding his fantasy outlook. He’s a late-round option at best.

 Center 
 #10 
 Khaman Maluach had 7 points (2-of-4 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 12 rebounds, a steal and a block against Jazz 
 Khaman Maluach is a good per minute producer while not demanding the ball. While he still can be raw, he’s improved to the point where he should play a role with Oso Ighodaro as the other center. He should be a good flyer in the back end of drafts.

 SAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #1 
 The Suns are starting Jamaree Bouyea, Luke Kennard, Ryan Dunn, Haywood Highsmith, and Khaman Maluach in Wednesday’s Exhibition against the Spurs. 
 The Suns are replacing Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks with Jamaree Bouyea and Haywood Highsmith from last Saturday’s exhibition. Jordan Goodwin will come off the bench as well. 
 Khaman Maluach 
 PHX 
 Center 
 #10 
 Khaman Maluach amassed 10 points (4-of-9 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), 15 rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s exhibition against the Spurs. 
 After coming off the bench in the Suns’ first two exhibition games, Maluach received the starting nod on Saturday. The second-year center held his own, leading all players with 15 rebounds while also recording a double-double. Oso Ighodaro (8/4/5/2/2) was the replacement in the starting lineup last season when Mark Williams missed time, but many believe Maluach offers a higher fantasy ceiling. He’s worth grabbing with a late-round pick in drafts, with the potential to deliver more value if Maluach earns the starting center role. 
 Oso Ighodaro 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #11 
 Oso Ighodaro finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bulls with eight points (4-of-6 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal. 
 The Suns have played two preseason games, and Ighodaro started both at center. While this may disappoint fans hoping to see Khaman Maluach (six points, seven rebounds and four assists) take the reins with Mark Williams (shoulder) injured, Oso starting isn’t a major surprise. He started 24 of the Suns’ 82 games last season and appears better equipped than Maluach to help the Suns immediately. However, Ighodaro starting the first two games doesn’t mean the final decision is made. This position battle is worth tracking through the rest of the preseason. 
 Khaman Maluach 
 PHX 
 Center 
 #10 
 Khaman Maluach scored six points (3-of-5 FGs, 0-for-3 FTs), two rebounds and one block over 16 minutes in Monday’s preseason loss to the Pistons. 
 Maluach played nearly 10 minutes off the bench alongside Phoenix’s main rotation players in the first half, which is notable given he’s likely in line for an expanded role behind Oso Ighodaro while Mark Williams recovers from shoulder surgery. The 20-year-old former lottery pick enters his second season as a viable rotation piece as an interior defender who can help Phoenix defensively without being a non-factor at the other end of the floor. He’ll be a late-round option in most fantasy leagues, but Maluach is a name to watch early in the season to see whether his role expands.

 Graham Ike accounted for 12 points (5-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
 Starting for the second consecutive game, Ike looked more comfortable than he did in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. Of course, while Suns center Khaman Maluach is listed at 7-foot-1, he isn’t as big as Memphis’ Zach Edey, which may have made things easier for Ike. The rookie out of Gonzaga, who’s on a two-way contract, recorded his first double-double and played 26 minutes. While Ike doesn’t need to be added in redraft leagues, dynasty league managers should stash him if possible.

 De’Anthony Melton finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 25 points (8-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and four three-pointers.
 Melton didn’t start Saturday’s game, but Stephen Curry’s and Brandin Podziemski’s absences gave him more opportunities. Melton took advantage, scoring 25 points, the most he’s scored in a game since 27 against the Wizards on March 16. Add in the rebounds, assists and steals, and Saturday night was a good one for fantasy managers who slotted Melton into their lineups.

 Brandon Williams tallied 20 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
 With Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski sitting out the second game of Golden State’s back-to-back, Williams and Will Richard (11 points, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers) were inserted into the starting lineup on Saturday. After shooting 4-of-17 in Golden State’s first two games, Williams was much more efficient against the Suns. His fantasy value will depend on the schedule going forward, and the Warriors end their four-game Week 2 with another back-to-back.

 Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, five assists, one block and six three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
 In the first week of the 2026-27 season, Lendeborg has been among the NBA’s most productive rookies. After recording his first double-double in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies, the Warriors forward notched his first 20-point game on Saturday. Lendeborg shot 6-of-11 from three, and his 19 shot attempts were the most on the team. Golden State didn’t have Stephen Curry, Draymond Green or Brandin Podziemski on Saturday, which opened things up for Lendeborg. However, the first two games showed that he’ll have a prominent role even when those key veterans are available.

 Luke Kennard produced 11 points (4-of-6 FGs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Warriors.
 Kennard made his Suns debut on Saturday after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, providing welcome three-point production. He shot 3-of-5 from beyond the arc against the Warriors, and his final stat line lacked only a blocked shot. Kennard can help managers who need points and three-pointers, but not while the Suns are on a light schedule. Phoenix plays two games in Week 2, so adding Kennard offers little upside.

 Collin Gillespie finished Saturday’s win over the Warriors with 11 points (4-of-7 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals and two three-pointers.
 After a brutal shooting night in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, going 0-of-8 from the field and failing to score, Gillespie got back on track Saturday night. He scored 11 points and recorded a team-high nine assists. Over two games, Gillespie has also recorded six steals. The negative for fantasy managers is the Suns’ schedule. After playing two games in Week 1, they’re the only NBA team that will play two games in Week 2. That takes some of the luster off of Gillespie in fantasy leagues.

 After scoring 23 points in the Suns’ season-opening loss to the Trail Blazers, Booker nearly doubled that output on Saturday. The Suns’ star guard shot 68 percent from the field and added strong rebounding and assist numbers. With the Suns playing just two games in Week 1, fantasy managers rostering Booker needed a night like this. The Suns have another bad schedule in Week 2, with only two games.
